*Speaking as the farmer:*

Alright, let me think through this year. Five mu isn't much — my wife and I work it together, and our son is working in the county town now, so it's just the two of us most days. I've been doing this 30 years, I know this land.

**My split this year**: I'm keeping about 2 mu for cotton on the sandier plot — that's been my cotton ground for years, it doesn't do great for wheat anyway. The other 3 mu I'll do wheat-maize double crop like always. The wheat gives us flour to eat and some to sell, and the maize I sell to the feed buyer. Cotton is my cash crop when the price is decent.

**Wheat** (3 mu, going in this October, but I'm still harvesting last year's and planning now): I'll use Jimai variety again — my neighbor Lao Wang tried that new drought-tolerant one last year, didn't do any better than mine, so I'll stick with what works. Base fertilizer about 30 kg of compound (15-15-15) per mu before plowing, then topdress about 10 kg urea at greening in spring. The extension guy at the township station keeps telling us 15 kg N is enough, but I usually do a touch more — better too much than too little, if it yellows I've lost real money. Irrigate at winter before the freeze, once at greening, once at grain fill. That's three times if the rain cooperates, four if it doesn't.

**Maize** (3 mu, straight after wheat harvest in mid-June — very tight window): Hybrid seed from the agro-store, Zhengdan 958 type, everyone around here plants it. No time to plow properly after wheat, I'll use the no-till planter — I don't own one, pay Old Liu 30 yuan per mu to come through with his machine. One base fertilizer application, compound plus some urea mixed in, maybe topdress urea at big trumpet stage if it looks pale. Usually one irrigation in July if it's dry. Herbicide after planting for grass.

**Cotton** (2 mu): This is the one that eats my labor. Plant mid-late April after the soil warms up. I use the local improved variety, save some seed but buy fresh most years. Fertilize heavier at the base — cotton eats a lot — and topdress once at flowering. Irrigate twice, once at squaring and once at boll-filling. The hard part is bollworm and aphids — I'll spray insecticide 3-4 times across the season, whatever I see at the market that others are using. Picking is the killer — takes my wife and me weeks, and we hire two village women for about 10 days when the main flush comes. Cotton price has been okay but not great, so I'm not expanding.

**Cash situation**: I've got maybe 4,000 yuan set aside for inputs. That's tight but manageable. If the cotton price drops bad this year, I might shift to more maize next year. I'm not gonna go into debt for fertilizer.
